purpose: Bootstrap mature outward-facing drafts for Parts 2 through 12 of the MCRP distributed-review sequence.
audience: Technically literate researchers, research-software practitioners, reviewers, and scholarly-infrastructure builders.
outline: Complete the core MCRP lifecycle: claim paths, authority, and freshness.
Decompose journal functions and introduce portable review records.
Describe federated attestation discovery as established guiding infrastructure.
Develop plural reputation, living-network automation, and distributed work routing.
Preserve disagreement, audit failure modes, and close with an evaluation contract.
retrieval_capability: bounded primary-source landscape already assembled; no new research-librarian retrieval required for seed prose
bibliography_inputs: W3C Linked Data Notifications, Activity Streams 2.0, and WebSub
human_questions: Which part should become the next outward-facing publication after the full private sequence is mature?
What cadence should the outward sequence use?
constraints: Publication and deployment require explicit human approval.
Trust registries and component standards are guiding prior art, not originality claims.
Automation may update records and derived views but may not silently grant human scientific authority.
Every public post must distinguish sourced background, proposed design, and unvalidated expected benefit.
excluded_claims: MCRP solves trust or establishes scientific truth.
MCRP has demonstrated interoperability, scale, governance legitimacy, capture resistance, or better review outcomes.
A signature or registry receipt proves competence, independence, or scientific adequacy.
